title: Napoleon's 1812 Russian Retreat & The Tin Button Disaster
overlooked_twist: The Grande Armée was not destroyed primarily by Russian bayonets. Sub-zero blizzards triggered 'tin pest'—an allotropic disintegration of cheap tin uniform buttons into gray powder—forcing freezing soldiers to clutch their coats with one hand while typhus-carrying body lice decimated 400,000 men.
primary_sources: General Armand de Caulaincourt (With Napoleon in Russia)
Philippe-Paul de Ségur (History of the Expedition to Russia)
wikipedia_summary: The French invasion of Russia began on 24 June 1812 when Napoleon's Grande Armée crossed the Neman River. The campaign was a catastrophic defeat for France; of an initial force of over 600,000 men, fewer than 100,000 returned alive, primarily lost to starvation, extreme sub-zero weather, and disease during the winter retreat.
